Week of 2026-08-27

The Investor's Podcast (formerly We Study Billionaires)
Host: Stig Brodersen, William Green, Shawn O'Malley, Daniel Mahncke, Kyle Grieve
Why for Fred: The direct, dedicated home for Buffett/Berkshire principles that his current lineup only touches in passing -- recent completed episodes on Diary of a CEO (Ray Dalio) and Invest Like the Best show he's actively pulling on this thread. Where Invest Like the Best ranges across all of investing, this show is narrower and deeper: dissecting individual Buffett/Munger/Dalio/Howard Marks letters and case studies, with William Green (author of Richer, Wiser, Happier) bringing the same "study the masters" lens Fred already applies via Business Breakdown-style teardown analysis.
Format: Long-form interview + solo teaching episodes, 2-3x/week, ~45-75 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode breaking down a Buffett shareholder letter or a Howard Marks memo -- check the feed for the latest
Link: https://www.theinvestorspodcast.com/the-investors-podcast-show/

Yet Another Value Podcast
Host: Andrew Walker
Why for Fred: World of Short Selling (suggested previously) covers the short side; this is the long-side complement for the same event-driven, special-situations niche that Pender Fund and Behind the Balance Sheet gesture at but don't centre -- busted compounders, spin-offs, weird capital structures, and activist situations, pitched by the fund managers actually holding the position. Recent 2026 episodes (Alex Roepers of Atlantic Investment Management on Dauch and Nomad Foods; Pershing Square Challenge pitches) are exactly the kind of concrete, numbers-first idea generation the MOI Global-adjacent thread of the wiki already favours.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: The Alex Roepers episode on Dauch (DCH) and Nomad Foods (NOMD) -- two live deep-value special situations argued in detail
Link: https://www.yetanothervalueblog.com/s/yet-another-value-podcast

The Genius Life
Host: Max Lugavere
Why for Fred: The Peter Attia Drive, Health Longevity Secrets, Dementia Matters, and FoundMyFitness (all previously suggested) approach dementia prevention from the physician/researcher side; Lugavere comes at the identical territory from a science-journalist-turned-advocate angle, driven by his own mother's dementia diagnosis, making the material more narrative and practically actionable rather than purely clinical. A February 2026 brain-health AMA covers dementia prevention, memory, and supplement protocols directly.
Format: Long-form interview + solo Q&A, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: "The Alzheimer's Fraud That Derailed Research for Decades" (Ep. 244, with Matt Bilinsky)
Link: https://www.maxlugavere.com/podcast/244

The AI Daily Brief
Host: Nathaniel Whittemore (NLW)
Why for Fred: The Cognitive Revolution (previously suggested) already fills part of the "staying current" gap, but at biweekly ~60-90 min episodes it can't match model-release velocity; AI Daily Brief runs near-daily at ~20 minutes, functioning as a running news ticker across inference economics, enterprise AI adoption, and startup funding -- the same threads spread across Fred's more analytical AI shows (Dwarkesh, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI), compressed into a briefing rather than a deep-dive commitment.
Format: News/analysis briefing, near-daily cadence, ~20 min
Sample episode: Any recent episode reacting to a frontier model release or major AI funding round
Link: https://aidailybrief.ai/

Week of 2026-08-06

Training Data
Host: Sonya Huang & Pat Grady (Sequoia Capital)
Why for Fred: His AI list (Dwarkesh, MLST, No Priors, Latent Space, Me Myself and AI, The Cognitive Revolution) is heavy on research, engineering, and enterprise-operator angles but light on venture capital's view of where AI startups and compute economics are heading. Huang and Grady sit inside Sequoia's own portfolio decisions, and 2026 episodes with Greg Brockman (OpenAI's full stack) and ElevenLabs' Mati Staniszewski map directly onto the AI-startups and inference-trends threads from the capital-deployment side.
Format: Long-form interview, weekly, ~45-60 min
Sample episode: Greg Brockman (AI Ascent 2026) -- the OpenAI stack, from research to product
Link: https://sequoiacap.com/podcasts/

Forward Guidance
Host: Felix Jauvin (Blockworks)
Why for Fred: Bankless, Epicenter, Empire, On The Margin, and Unchained have all been suggested without being picked up -- all approach DeFi from inside crypto-native media. Forward Guidance is a macro show first, with crypto as one asset class among several: Jauvin interviews the same tier of macro strategists as Behind the Balance Sheet and Hidden Forces about rates, fiscal policy, and the K-shaped economy, then extends the framework to digital assets and stablecoins.
Format: Long-form interview + weekly roundup, weekly, ~45-75 min
Sample episode: Vincent Deluard on the "three-bubble thesis" for 2026 -- fiscal stimulus, a second inflation wave, and the Fed's path under Kevin Warsh
Link: https://blockworks.co/podcast/forwardguidance

FoundMyFitness
Host: Dr. Rhonda Patrick, PhD
Why for Fred: The Peter Attia Drive, Health Longevity Secrets, and Dementia Matters (all previously suggested) cover longevity/dementia from a physician's clinical-trial lens; Patrick -- a biomedical scientist by training -- comes at the same territory from the mechanistic-research side, translating primary literature on vitamin D, sauna, and fasting into specific protocols, with a running dementia-risk thread more granular than the broader longevity shows already on the list.
Format: Long-form interview + solo research deep-dives, weekly, ~60-90 min
Sample episode: The July 2026 episode on glucosamine, Alzheimer's risk, and creatine -- most direct overlap with existing listening
Link: https://www.foundmyfitness.com/episodes

Nudge
Host: Phill Agnew
Why for Fred: Choiceology and Behavioral Grooves (both previously suggested) cover behavioral economics from an academic/research angle; Nudge is the applied-marketing counterpart -- the UK's top-ranked marketing podcast, translating specific psychological effects (loss aversion, scarcity, framing) into concrete campaign and pricing decisions, with guests like Rory Sutherland and Richard Shotton. Direct Seth Godin/marketing-psychology lane in Fred's profile neither prior behavioral-economics suggestion actually addresses head-on.
Format: Interview, weekly, ~20-30 min
Sample episode: Any episode featuring Richard Shotton or Rory Sutherland -- the sharpest practitioner-side guests on framing and pricing psychology
Link: https://www.nudgepodcast.com/
